items.title: Quest Diagnostics confirms data breach exposed patient records
items.snippet: American clinical laboratory company Quest Diagnostics disclosed that patient records have been exposed after a threat actor gained unauthorized access to its Quanum LSM system. [...]
items.summary: Quest Diagnostics disclosed that patient records were exposed after a threat actor gained unauthorized access to its Quanum LSM system.
items.why: Review access to Quanum LSM and check whether patient data or related systems require investigation.

items.title: FCC bans two devices with surveillance chips linked to Huawei
items.snippet: The banned items — a wireless video transmitter and dashboard camera — are made with chips manufactured by Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon, which markets its products as “designed for the surveillance market.”
items.summary: The FCC banned a wireless video transmitter and dashboard camera made with chips from Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon, which markets them for surveillance.
items.why: Check whether the named devices are present in organizational equipment inventories.

items.title: Microsoft: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in January
items.snippet: Microsoft says Windows Server 2016 will stop receiving security updates after it reaches the end of support in January 2027. [...]
items.summary: Microsoft says Windows Server 2016 will stop receiving security updates after reaching end of support in January 2027.
items.why: Identify Windows Server 2016 systems and plan for support ending.

items.title: PHP shares mitigation for new RCE vulnerability with no patch
items.snippet: The PHP security team has shared mitigation measures for a new remote code execution vulnerability that affects systems with non-default configurations and has no patch. [...]
items.summary: The PHP security team shared mitigation measures for a new remote code execution vulnerability affecting non-default configurations; no patch is available.
items.why: Check whether PHP systems use non-default configurations and apply the security team’s mitigation measures.

items.summary: Gen Digital says malicious emails, websites, and plugins can manipulate AI agents into executing commands, stealing data, or deleting files using their legitimate permissions.

items.title: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts
items.snippet: Japanese gaming giant Capcom has confirmed that hackers breached its membership service, CAPCOM ID, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses and associated information. [...]
items.summary: Capcom confirms hackers breached its CAPCOM ID membership service, exposing customer email addresses and associated information.
items.why: Review account data exposure and notify affected users through established incident-response processes.

items.title: UK proposes 14-year prison terms for undersea cable sabotage
items.snippet: In an era of hybrid threats, the British government wants to update the Submarine Telegraph Act 1885, which carries a maximum fine of £1,000 and five years’ imprisonment in cases of deliberate damage.
items.summary: The British government proposes updating a law on deliberate undersea cable damage, which currently carries a maximum fine of £1,000 and five years’ imprisonment.
items.why: Undersea cables are critical infrastructure; consider their security and resilience in risk planning.

The bugs lie behind four critical security flaws that GitLab patched over the past month. GitLab found that a specially crafted pattern could corrupt memory while Ruby compiles it, po

items.title: Denmark To Buy Anthem Munitions, Joint Strike Missiles In Dual Long-Range Strike Push
items.snippet: The ground- and air-launched weapons will give Denmark all-new options for striking deep behind enemy lines as NATO reinforces its Baltic flank. The post Denmark To Buy Anthem Munitions, Joint Strike Missiles In Dual Long-Range Strike Push appeared first on TWZ .
items.summary: The War Zone reports Denmark plans to buy ground- and air-launched Anthem Munitions and Joint Strike Missiles for long-range strike options.

items.snippet: “This is a significant achievement, particularly as we continue to expand Qatar’s domestic defence and security capabilities in a year where we have had to rise to a number of regional challenges,” the company said in a statement.
items.summary: Qatari Barzan unveiled aerial drones and unmanned surface vessels at Milipol 2026. The company says the display reflects efforts to expand Qatar’s domestic defence and security capabilities.
items.why: The systems are relevant to Qatar’s domestic defence and security capabilities.

items.title: Natilus secures Air Force contract to develop blended wing body aircraft
items.snippet: “We think now’s the right time” for a blended wing body design to make its debut, Natilus Chief Operating Officer Nolan Giblin told Breaking Defense.
items.summary: Natilus secured an Air Force contract to develop a blended wing body aircraft. Its chief operating officer told Breaking Defense the company thinks it is the right time for the design to debut.
items.why: The contract advances development of a blended wing body aircraft.

items.title: ‘The West can’t stop me’: Space wars heat up as Russia tails a Ukraine-linked US satellite
items.snippet: Washington blamed Moscow for deliberately moving a Russian military satellite with an undisclosed mission close last week to a U.S.-registered satellite.
items.summary: Washington blamed Moscow for deliberately moving a Russian military satellite with an undisclosed mission close to a U.S.-registered satellite.

items.title: France, UK carry out joint airborne nuclear-strike exercise for first time
items.snippet: “This is a revolution for the Strategic Air Forces, which have always operated in complete autonomy since their creation in the 1960s,” said one analyst.
items.summary: France and the UK carried out a joint airborne nuclear-strike exercise for the first time. An analyst called it a revolution for the Strategic Air Forces.

items.title: US Air Force wants AI to assist aerial refueling

items.title: Leonardo, Rheinmetall secure $4 billion contracts with Italian Army, report says

items.summary: An Italian financial newspaper reported that Leonardo and Rheinmetall secured two Italian Army contracts for armored vehicles.

items.title: Saudi missile plant expansion may produce more powerful missiles, study says

learn.explainer: A CISA catalog of vulnerabilities with evidence of active exploitation. Defenders can use it to identify issues that may need prompt remediation.
A military strike option intended to reach targets far from the launching position. The Denmark report describes ground- and air-launched weapons as providing such options.

analysis.headline: Access, exposure and security across connected systems
paragraphs: The cyber stories point to different ways systems and data can be put at risk: Quest disclosed unauthorized access and exposed patient records, while Microsoft describes credential theft and remote code loading in the LiteLLM compromise. CISA’s KEV addition also makes active exploitation a practical prioritization concern.

For defenders, these reports suggest checking access controls, credentials, affected software and asset inventories. The Windows Server 2016 support deadline adds a lifecycle task; the FCC device ban makes equipment provenance and inventory relevant too. These items describe distinct issues, not a shared cause.

The Black Sea report shifts attention to physical security near Romanian waters: a drone hit a ship, with casualties reported. Denmark’s planned long-range strike purchases also show changing military options on NATO’s Baltic flank. Analysts should watch how these separate cyber, equipment and maritime developments evolve.
takeaways: Investigate access to systems holding sensitive records.
Use CISA’s KEV Catalog to guide remediation checks.
Track maritime incidents and changing long-range strike options.
